title: Broomstick lace vest
excerpt: An oversized mesh vest in DK yarn worked in broomstick lace. Two matching panels are seamed at the shoulders and sides with armhole openings left unworked.
sourceNotes: Two broomstick lace panels seamed to form a simple drop-shoulder vest. Armholes are shaped by leaving the upper sides open, and a double crochet edging finishes the neck and arms.

glossaryTerms.definition: A simple garment construction where the sleeve opening is created by leaving the upper sides unjoined. There is no armhole shaping in the panels.
The join across the top of a vest connecting front and back panels, worked with whip stitch through the bound-off edges.

crochet.gaugeText: 3 clusters (15 sts) x 5 rows = 10 cm in broomstick lace on 4.0 mm hook.
crochet.finishedSizeText: Fits bust 90 to 100 cm. Finished width 55 cm per panel.

and lower sides, with the upper sides left open as armholes.
Chain 85. Row 1: dc in each ch (85 dc). Do not turn. Work broomstick lace in groups of 5 (17 clusters) until the panel measures 60 cm. Bind off.
Place panels right sides out with top edges aligned. Sew a 15 cm shoulder seam at each top corner. Sew the lower 25 cm of each side edge together, leaving 20 cm open for the armhole.
Work 1 round of dc around the neck opening and each armhole. Fasten off and weave in the ends with the tapestry needle.
